decision: Scan = 'Lexus 4IS IS350 Full Car.stl' (Drive 1IOKNZ0p...) + 'Lexus 4IS reflector'/'reflector removed' (2025-07-17); NOT the '2026 IS350 Facelift' folder
why: Footage (FX3A, 2025-07-11) shows plate 9JTY488 and the pre-facelift mesh spindle grille; the full-car scan's plate reads 9JTY488 and has the same grille. The 2026 Facelift front-end scan has a different bumper/grille (different car), so none of its state scans can be used for this car

decision: Footage camera = Sony ILME-FX3A (full frame, 35.6 mm sensor width) + FE 24-70mm F2.8 GM II, S-Log3/S-Gamut3.Cine, 3840x2160 23.976p
why: Read from the FX305xxM01.XML sidecars (brief said FX30). Zoom lens and no focal length in the XML, so focal must come from per-frame metadata or be solved; S-Log3 needs a Rec709 LUT (lut/slog3_709.cube, Hable)

decision: Scan prep: decimate 4 mm (24.9M->4.1M tris) -> tools/level.py (RANSAC ground plane + yaw, copied from huracan-evo; same transform for reflector scans) -> ive crop -> tools/clean.py -> ive prep --drop-islands 3000 => scan/car.blend
why: The Artec frame was tilted ~3.5 deg and yawed ~9 deg; unlevelled, ive crop left a ground flap in front of the bumper. Cleaned footprint 4,699 x 1,848 mm vs IS350 spec length 4,710 mm

decision: No panel/bumper removal exists in the footage (all 15 clips checked: 541 keyframes every 1 s, 550 at 2 fps, others by sheet). Section 2 = crew scanning with the handheld scanner, 1:1 cut on a rear handheld-scanning frame, then the scan pops the rear reflector out
why: Brief asked for a panel/bumper removal + part-state cut; the only part-state scans for this car are 'Lexus 4IS reflector' / 'reflector removed' (2025-07-17) and no clip shows it being removed. 550 shows the rear being jacked up (changes ride height - not a usable match state)

decision: Opening 1:1 match = FX30554 @ 11.011 s (frame 264, front 3/4 outside the shop door), scan = full car; cam_A2 = 7-point PnP (plate corners, mirror tips; emblem dropped) + silhouette refine (tools/refine.py, GrabCut), focal 32.6 mm on the 35.6 mm FX3A sensor
why: Camera walks out of the shop into daylight and settles on the whole car (bumper/hood on = full-car scan state). Free focal solve landed at 32.4 mm (inside the 24-70 zoom), roof sat 20 px high until the silhouette refine; onion now aligns grille, emblem, plate, lamps, mirrors and roofline

decision: Second 1:1 match = FX30542 frame 1135 (47.339 s): crew member crouched at the rear, scanner raised to the bumper; scan = full car; cam_B = 11-point PnP (plate screws/frame, emblem, IS350 badge, right exhaust, 3 diffuser fins), focal 31.1 mm, RMSE 4.1 px
why: Handheld rear scanning is the real action; the pan is slowest here (~1.6 px/frame) just before a whip at 47.5 s. Plate screws (178 mm apart = 7-inch US plate holes) are precise landmarks; onion aligns plate, emblem, exhausts, fins and bumper edges

decision: Music = the generated IS350 track, started on kick 26 (13.056 s) so the drop (kick 32, highs +10 dB after a 1-beat kick break) lands at 3.000 s; 16 beats (kick 40-56) repeated once; video beat n = 0.50004 n s
why: Kick-peak grid t=0.0545+0.50004k (40-120 Hz, 3 ms rms, 120 BPM). Starting 6 kicks before the drop gives the walk-out shot a real percussive bed and puts the 1:1 cut ON the drop (lessons: hook + no cuts on a quiet build). The track's post-drop section is only 16 s; the repeat makes room for scan + reassembly + website (27 s). Output re-checked: every kick within +-2 ms of the grid across both splices

decision: Real clips pre-rendered with tools/irl.py (S-Log3 LUT, 9:16 window from the 4K original, 23.976->30 fps anchored so the last frame IS the match frame): i1 554 f193-264 x0 596 (3.0 s); i2 549 f25-48 powder spray (1.0 s); i3 547 f1175-1210 scanner screen live-scanning (1.5 s); i4 542 f1052-1135 rear scan, digital pan x0 760->40 over the last 58% (3.5 s)
why: assemble only centre-crops after scaling and applies the LUT late; doing the crop at 4K keeps detail and lets the match crop be exact. The rear pan starts on the crew + scanner and settles on the left-rear corner (the scanned reflector) so the scan can pop that part out

decision: S2 scan_rear: 1:1 from camP_B (cam_B in the x0=40 crop), base = full car with the reflector zone (+40 mm) replaced by the 'reflector removed' scan (tools/splice.py); reflector pops out (+0.15,+0.65,-0.12 m, 8-40 %) into the black below the bumper, then spins 360 deg about Z (38-95 %); camera lowers 0.25 m
why: Pull/push would zoom toward the lens-shifted optical centre (off the right of the crop) and slide the car out of frame; a vertical move has no zoom. Silver part over the silver bumper had no contrast - below the bumper it reads on black (~200 px). Z spin per 240SX feedback (left/right, not flips); the reflector scan has both the lens face and the clip side, so inside+outside is true

decision: Listing camera (cam_L2): illumaesthetic.com 'Lexus IS (XE30) 3D Scan (Facelift, 2020+)' 360-viewer default view, solved by silhouette fit on a luminance mask of the viewer canvas (x 275-1725, y 367-1310 of the 2880x1640 screenshot): chamfer 0.3 px @700, f 47.9 mm/36
why: The viewer model is this same scan (same empty rear wheel well). GrabCut grabbed background above the roof; a threshold mask on the flat dark canvas is exact. Ending the x-ray on this pose makes the dissolve into the listing read as one object (240SX lesson)

decision: S3 scan_xray (tools/path_render.py = scan_render with a two-camera move): starts on S2's last pose (camP_B lowered 0.25 m) so S2->S3 is a look change at the same angle on the beat; reflector translates home (0-50 %), camera swoops out/around to camP_L (listing pose mapped into the WebZoom first frame, focus 960,880, startScale 1.245); x-ray morphs to listing-grey clay 72-95 %
why: A full-car x-ray makes the 11 cm reflector ~20 px - its reassembly would be invisible; starting close and pulling out keeps it readable, and ending exactly on the listing's 360-viewer pose makes the dissolve read as one object. Clay/bg tuned from medians (listing car 136, bg 23-26)

decision: Reflector splice redone by surface distance (tools/splice.py: drop full-car faces <8 mm from the reflector scan, add 'reflector removed' faces >8 mm from the remaining car within bbox+30 mm)
why: The bbox+40 mm box splice exposed a black coverage hole around the corner on S2's first frame (the state scan doesn't cover that much bumper) - lessons: splice over the smallest zone

decision: Verified 'INSIDE + OUTSIDE' for the reflector on the rendered S2 frames (spin shows the lens face, then the clip/back side); HUD labels moved to y 0.66
why: Only claim what the render shows (lessons). The part settles lower (~y 0.85) than planned, so the labels go in the black above it instead of over the part or the silver body

decision: HUD: counter value 25,024,430 so the ScanHUD count-up ENDS on the true 24,999,992 (STL header); reflector labels right-aligned at y 0.72 from frame 414
why: ScanHUD's counter uses Easing.out(exp), which stops at 1-2^-10 = 99.9 % of value (it showed 24,975,578 - a wrong number on screen; the 240SX reel had the same bug). Labels at left/0.86 sat on the falling reflector; at 0.72 right they are on black once the camera lowers
